Philosophy of Religion: Problems of Evil & Suffering — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.

mcqs.q: What distinction matters for the free will defence to the problem of evil?
options: Between moral evil (caused by free human choices) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease) — the free will defence directly addresses moral evil but struggles with natural evil, which isn't a product of free choice.
Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
The free will defence solves all forms of evil at once.

mcqs.q: Mackie's inconsistent triad consists of the propositions:
options: God is omnipotent; God is wholly good; evil exists
God is omniscient; God is eternal; suffering exists
evil is real; evil is an illusion; evil is a privation
God exists; free will exists; natural laws exist

mcqs.q: In the Augustinian tradition, evil entered the world through:
options: the free choices of angels and humans in the Fall
God's deliberate creation of evil
an evil power equal and opposite to God
the inherent wickedness of matter itself

mcqs.q: Hick's affirmation of universal salvation functions in his theodicy to:
options: guarantee that the suffering involved in soul-making is ultimately justified for everyone
show that hell is the necessary destiny of the wicked
prove that suffering is an illusion
remove the need for human freedom

mcqs.q: In the Irenaean tradition developed by Hick, evil and suffering are:
options: necessary conditions of a world in which souls can grow toward the likeness of God
a privation of good with no purpose
proof that God is limited in power
punishments inherited from Adam's guilt
